title: Prompt Perturbation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Language Models

problem.claim: The work studies the robustness of retrieval-augmented generation outputs to slightly different prompt inputs.

gap.claim: The effect of slightly different inputs on outputs from RAG-based LLMs is not well studied.

contributions.claim: The authors introduce Gradient Guided Prompt Perturbation (GGPP), an optimization technique for systematically evaluating and steering the effects of prompt prefixes on RAG-based LLMs.
The authors develop a detector based on neuron activation differences triggered by GGPP-generated prompts to improve the robustness of RAG-based LLMs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GGPP as a novel optimization technique.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that inserting even a short prefix can lead RAG-based LLMs to produce outputs far from factually correct answers.
The authors report that GGPP achieves a high success rate in steering RAG-based LLM outputs toward targeted wrong answers and can handle instructions to ignore irrelevant context.
The authors report that evaluations on open-sourced LLMs demonstrate the effectiveness of their methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Robustness is important as LLM use expands, and RAG is used to improve trustworthiness.
The effect of small prompt-input changes on RAG-based LLM outputs is insufficiently studied.
Short prompt prefixes can cause outputs to depart substantially from factually correct answers.
GGPP is introduced to evaluate and steer prompt perturbation effects, alongside a neuron-activation-based robustness detector.
The methods are evaluated on open-sourced LLMs, with effectiveness reported by the authors.

source_observation.claim: Small prompt changes, including short prefixes, can substantially alter the factuality of RAG-based LLM outputs.

interpretation.claim: Prompt robustness should be treated as a potential failure surface in retrieval-augmented generation.

application.claim: RAG evaluations and deployments could include prompt-perturbation testing and detectors based on activation changes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how broadly these effects generalize across models, datasets, perturbations, or deployment settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated models, datasets, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe GGPP's optimization procedure or detector training details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or full-text experimental conditions.
